description: Interactive step-based equation builder for Grade 7 Mathematics — Number Machine Formula Detective. Students discover hidden formulas by observing input-output pairs from 3 progressively harder number machines (Formula Factories). Features Y-shaped machine graphic with dual-colour input funnels (purple for a, orange for b), animated number tokens, candidate formula testing workspace, and verification tables. Built on the Singularity design system with Poppins font and purple-orange palette.
topic: Formula Detective and Saree Border Patterns
subject: Mathematics
learningObjectives: Develop systematic trial-and-test thinking for algebraic pattern discovery
Understand how algebraic expressions represent operations on two inputs
Learn to verify a formula by substituting multiple input-output pairs
Progress from simple (2a − b) to complex (3a − b + 1) formula recognition

teachingNotes.machine1: For Machine 1, suggest students start with simple operations (a + b, a − b, a × b) and then try combinations like 2a − b.
teachingNotes.machine2: Emphasise that the SAME inputs (5, 2) give a DIFFERENT output from Machine 1, so the formula must be different.
teachingNotes.machine3: Hint that the formula might include a constant (a number without a variable).
teachingNotes.afterAll: Ask: What strategy did you use to discover the formulas? Can you make your own number machine and challenge a friend? Connect to the saree border pattern where the remainder method uses a similar systematic approach.
teachingNotes.connectionToSaree: In the saree border pattern (Example 12 in textbook), designs A, B, C repeat every 3 positions. The positions are described by 3n−2, 3n−1, and 3n — this is the same systematic pattern-finding approach used in the Formula Detective.
hints: 💡 Start with simple operations like a + b, a − b, then try 2a − b.
💡 Same inputs (5, 2) give a DIFFERENT output. The formula must differ from Machine 1!
💡 This formula might include a constant — a number without a variable!

instructions_for_student: You are a Formula Detective! Each number machine takes two inputs (a and b) and produces an output using a secret formula. Your job is to figure out the formula. Watch the input-output pairs being revealed, try different formulas in your head, and see if your guess matches all the pairs. The machines get harder — the third one has a constant term in the formula!

customMachines.description: Pass custom machines array to override defaults

minimalUI.description: Hide navigation and step indicator for embedded use
